newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy easing seen by May, may be last one.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy easing seen by May, may be last one.

text.p: Italian monetary authorities might take another slice off official interest rates in the next month but many economists believe this will be the last easing in the cycle, a Reuter poll showed.

On average 10 out of 12 analysts in Milan and London, polled at the start of the week, forecast a 50 to 75 basis points easing which would bring the official discount rate to 6.25/6.0 percent from the current 6.75 percent.

"The conditions for a cut already exist but they will be emphasized by the end of April after inflation data from 11 sample cities which could come in under two percent," Gianluca Sanna, economist at Stone & McCarthy said.

Deutsche Bank said economic conditions existed for a cut and the government's mini-budget unveiled in March would allow Italy's budget deficit to gross domestic product ratio to fall to the three percent needed to join a single European currency.
Stefano Lelli, analyst at Banco di Sardegna saw a 75 basis point easing by the end of April or at the latest at the end of May when year-on-year inflation is forecast under two percent.
"The Bank of Italy could wait until May to cut rates because Italian financial markets are supported by the expectation of an interest rate cut," Lelli said.
Francesco Giordano, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston, had previously not forecast an easing but changed his outlook given "scarce signs of economic recovery in Italy."
State research group Isco's January economic survey had hinted at recovery but this was not confirmed by later data, Giordano said, adding this would be the last cut in the cycle.

Ken Wattret, economist at Paribas, saw the January rate cut as the last for this cycle, although he did not wholly dismiss another one if the lira held firm and stable, which he said was now more in the Bank of Italy's focus than falling prices.
Lucia Trevisan, analyst at Caboto, agreed saying she did not forecast a rate cut but could not entirely rule out the possibility given current dollar strength and the firmer lira.
Wattret argued however a potential U.S. rate rise in coming months could weaken U.S. markets and the dollar, which would have a knock-on effect on the lira.
Furthermore, economic data especially from Germany later in the year was likely to be positive and financial markets would start to ask when they could expect an interest rate hike.

Alfredo Granata at Banca di Roma saw a 50-75 basis point easing by the end of April, adding: "One cannot say if this will be the last rate cut because the EMU decision is based on economics up to a certain point, but then it becomes political."
"If the idea is that EMU will start with Italy in the first group, this will definitely not be the last rate cut. Otherwise it probably will be," he said.
Other analysts said Italian interest rates were closely linked to rates in the rest of Europe.

"In the fourth quarter, with an economic pick-up in Germany and Italy, Italian inflation and the official interest rate will start rising (putting the discount rate at 6.5 percent) and the interest rate cut cycle will be over," Lelli said.
"If German interest rates remain stable, the Bank of Italy will have the scope for a further easing by the end of the summer," Lorenzo Codogno, economist at Bank of America said.

But Stone & McCarthy's Sanna said: "Italy more than other European countries needs a very expansive monetary policy. CPI has not yet bottomed out and the economy doesn't show any pick-up signs. For some time there could be a decoupling of the U.S. interest rate cycle with the European rate cycle," he said.
Following are the results of the survey:
Do you forecast a further interest rate cut in Italy?
Yes (10 out of 12)
If yes, by how much will the Bank of Italy cut rates?
When will the Bank of Italy cut rates?
By the end of April (6/10)
By the end of May (3/10)
Within three months (1/10)
Will this be the last interest rate cut of the cycle?
Possibly (2/10)
The following bankis took part of the poll: Bank of America, Banca di Roma, Banco di Sardegna, BCI, Cariplo, Caboto, Chase, CSFB, Stone & McCarthy, UBS, Paribas, Deutsche Bank.
